checks.question: Are public endpoints, message schemas, exported functions, fields, enums, or behaviors changed in a breaking way without versioning or a backward-compatibility plan (breaking public API change without versioning)? (API-001)

onYes.title: Fix unversioned breaking API change (API-001): version or preserve compatibility
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Breaking a public contract without versioning breaks existing clients.

Find all instances: Search recent/changed public endpoints, schemas, exported signatures, fields, and enums for breaking changes lacking versioning or compatibility handling.

Fix correctly: Version the API (new version/endpoint) or preserve backward compatibility (additive changes, deprecate-then-remove). Provide a migration path.

Constraints: Don't break existing consumers. Follow the project's versioning conventions.

Acceptance: Public changes are versioned or backward-compatible. Add a contract test asserting old clients still work.

checks.question: Are schemas or DTOs duplicated across client, server, tests, and docs in a way that can drift (client/server schema mismatch)? (API-002)

onYes.title: Fix schema drift (API-002): generate/validate from one contract
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Duplicated, hand-maintained schemas drift apart, causing integration failures.

Find all instances: Search for duplicated request/response schemas/DTOs maintained separately on client, server, tests, and docs.

Fix correctly: Generate or validate all sides from a single source of truth (shared schema/IDL/contract).

Constraints: Add a drift check in CI (BLD-014).

Acceptance: Schemas derive from one contract. Add a test/check failing on client/server schema divergence.

checks.question: Does the implementation accept input values that the documented contract says are invalid (implementation accepts invalid documented input)? (API-003)

onYes.title: Fix contract-vs-validation gap (API-003): align validation with the contract
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Accepting input the contract forbids creates undefined behavior and security gaps.

Find all instances: Search endpoints where runtime validation is looser than the documented contract (formats, ranges, required fields).

Fix correctly: Align runtime validation with the public contract; reject documented-invalid input.

Constraints: Validate at the boundary; prefer allowlists. Keep the contract authoritative.

Acceptance: Runtime validation matches the contract. Add tests sending documented-invalid input proving rejection.

checks.question: Are fields documented as required returned as null/missing, or documented nullable but handled as required (response nullability mismatch)? (API-004)

onYes.title: Fix nullability mismatch (API-004): match response shape to docs
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Nullability mismatches crash clients or cause silent data gaps.

Find all instances: Search responses where required fields can be null/missing or nullable fields are assumed present (on both produce and consume sides).

Fix correctly: Make the runtime response match documented nullability; handle nullable fields defensively on the consuming side.

Constraints: Keep the contract authoritative; update docs if the real shape differs intentionally (with versioning).

Acceptance: Response nullability matches the contract. Add tests asserting required fields are always present and nullable fields are handled.

checks.question: Do APIs return different error shapes, field names, or code conventions across endpoints (inconsistent error response format)? (API-005)

onYes.title: Fix inconsistent error format (API-005): use one error envelope
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Inconsistent error formats force clients to special-case each endpoint and cause mishandling.

Find all instances: Search error responses across endpoints for differing shapes/field names/code conventions.

Fix correctly: Adopt a single machine-readable error envelope (consistent fields: code, message, details) and apply it everywhere.

Constraints: Don't leak internals (ERR-014). Keep codes stable.

Acceptance: Errors use a consistent envelope. Add tests asserting representative endpoints return the standard error shape.

checks.question: Do GET/HEAD methods mutate state, or are unsafe methods used for safe reads (HTTP method semantics violated)? (API-006)

onYes.title: Fix HTTP method semantics (API-006): keep safe methods side-effect-free
onYes.prompt:
Problem: State-changing GETs break caching/CSRF assumptions and can be triggered accidentally (prefetch, crawlers).

Find all instances: Search for GET/HEAD handlers with side effects and mutations using safe methods.

Fix correctly: Use POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE for mutations; keep GET/HEAD safe and idempotent.

Constraints: Coordinate with CSRF (IAM-017) and idempotency (API-011).

Acceptance: Method semantics are correct. Add a test asserting GET/HEAD cause no state change.

checks.question: Do responses use HTTP/gRPC/status codes that don't match the actual outcome (status code misuse)? (API-007)

onYes.title: Fix status code misuse (API-007): return accurate status codes
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Wrong status codes (e.g. 200 on error) break client error handling, retries, and monitoring.

Find all instances: Search responses where the status code doesn't reflect the outcome (success/client-error/server-error/auth/conflict).

Fix correctly: Return codes that accurately represent the outcome; map domain errors to correct codes consistently.

Constraints: Pair with consistent error envelope (API-005) and not-fabricating-success (ERR-003).

Acceptance: Status codes match outcomes. Add tests asserting correct codes for success, validation error, auth failure, not-found, and conflict.

checks.question: Do paginated APIs use unstable ordering, offset-only pagination, or cursors without a deterministic sort (unstable pagination cursor/sort)? (API-008)

onYes.title: Fix unstable pagination (API-008): deterministic ordering and opaque cursors
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Unstable ordering causes skipped/duplicated items across pages.

Find all instances: Search paginated endpoints for non-deterministic ordering or cursors lacking a stable sort.

Fix correctly: Use deterministic ordering with a unique tie-breaker and opaque cursor semantics; prefer keyset pagination.

Constraints: Coordinate with DAT-013 and PER-017.

Acceptance: Pagination is stable. Add a test paging through changing data asserting no skips/duplicates.

checks.question: Can page counts, cursors, totals, next/previous links, or has-more flags disagree (inconsistent pagination metadata)? (API-009)

onYes.title: Fix inconsistent pagination metadata (API-009): compute from one snapshot
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Pagination metadata computed from different queries/snapshots can contradict the returned items.

Find all instances: Search pagination responses where totals/cursors/has-more/links derive from separate queries or timing.

Fix correctly: Compute all pagination metadata consistently from the same query/snapshot as the returned items.

Constraints: Keep ordering stable (API-008).

Acceptance: Metadata agrees with results. Add a test asserting has-more/next-cursor/total are consistent with the page contents.

checks.question: Does client code ignore rate-limit responses, Retry-After headers, or quota errors (rate limit not handled)? (API-010)

onYes.title: Fix rate limit handling (API-010): respect Retry-After and backoff
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Ignoring rate limits causes cascading failures and bans.

Find all instances: Search outbound API clients for handling of 429/quota responses and Retry-After.

Fix correctly: Respect Retry-After, apply backoff with jitter, and honor quota semantics; surface persistent limiting.

Constraints: Bound retries (ERR-007). Retry only when appropriate (ERR-005).

Acceptance: Clients honor rate limits. Add a test simulating 429+Retry-After asserting correct backoff.

checks.question: Do APIs that clients may retry fail to define idempotency behavior (idempotency contract absent)? (API-011)

onYes.title: Fix missing idempotency contract (API-011): define idempotent retries
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Without a defined idempotency contract, client retries cause duplicate effects.

Find all instances: Search mutating endpoints that clients may retry for idempotency-key support and documented behavior.

Fix correctly: Define and enforce idempotency (accept an idempotency key; return the prior result on replay). Document the behavior.

Constraints: Implement server-side dedup (CON-016).

Acceptance: Retried mutations are idempotent. Add a test replaying with the same idempotency key asserting a single effect.

checks.question: Do clients crash or reject responses when receiving unknown future enum values (backward-incompatible enum handling)? (API-012)

onYes.title: Fix enum forward-compat (API-012): tolerate unknown enum values
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Strict enum parsing breaks clients when the server adds new enum values.

Find all instances: Search client deserialization of enums for hard failures on unknown values.

Fix correctly: Tolerate unknown enum values (map to an 'unknown/other' case) where forward compatibility is required.

Constraints: Still validate where an unknown value is genuinely invalid; this applies to forward-compatible reads.

Acceptance: Unknown enum values don't crash clients. Add a test deserializing an unknown enum value asserting graceful handling.

checks.question: Do APIs or clients reject unknown fields despite needing forward compatibility (unknown fields rejected unexpectedly)? (API-013)

onYes.title: Fix unknown-field rejection (API-013): preserve/ignore unknown fields per contract
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Rejecting unknown fields breaks forward compatibility when new fields are added.

Find all instances: Search deserialization configured to reject unknown/extra fields where forward compatibility is needed.

Fix correctly: Ignore (and preserve where round-tripping) unknown fields according to the contract's compatibility expectations.

Constraints: Where strictness is a deliberate security control (e.g. mass-assignment defense), keep it; this targets forward-compat reads, not authority fields (IAM-004).

Acceptance: Unknown fields are tolerated per contract. Add a test sending an extra field asserting it's ignored, not rejected.

checks.question: Do API responses serialize full internal models exposing secrets, PII, internal flags, or permissions (sensitive field exposed in API response)? (API-014)

onYes.title: Fix sensitive field exposure (API-014): use explicit response DTOs
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Serializing whole internal entities leaks secrets/PII/internal fields to clients.

Find all instances: Search response serialization that returns internal/domain models directly rather than curated DTOs.

Fix correctly: Define explicit response DTOs/views containing only approved fields; never serialize internal models directly.

Constraints: Prefer allowlists of exposed fields. Coordinate with CSP-002/CSP-017.

Acceptance: Responses expose only approved fields. Add a test asserting sensitive/internal fields are absent from responses.

checks.question: Does code make one remote API call per item in a loop where batch/bulk APIs are available (N+1 remote API call pattern)? (API-015)

onYes.title: Fix N+1 remote calls (API-015): batch, prefetch, or cache
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Per-item remote calls multiply latency and risk rate limits.

Find all instances: Search loops issuing one remote API/RPC call per element where bulk/batch endpoints exist.

Fix correctly: Batch, prefetch, cache, or reshape integration calls to reduce round trips.

Constraints: Bound batch size and concurrency (PER-007).

Acceptance: Per-item remote fan-out is eliminated. Add a test/check asserting a bounded number of calls for N items.

checks.question: Do diagnostic/health endpoints expose config, environment, dependency details, stack traces, or secrets (debug/health endpoint leaks internals)? (API-016)

onYes.title: Fix debug endpoint leakage (API-016): restrict and protect diagnostics
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Verbose diagnostic/health endpoints leak internal/sensitive details to attackers.

Find all instances: Search health/debug/diagnostic endpoints for exposure of config/env/dependency details/stack traces/secrets and for missing access control.

Fix correctly: Restrict detail in public endpoints, protect sensitive diagnostics behind auth, and separate liveness from detailed diagnostics.

Constraints: Don't leak secrets (CSP-002). Separate liveness/readiness (OPS-007).

Acceptance: Diagnostics don't leak internals and are access-controlled. Add a test asserting the public health endpoint exposes no sensitive detail.

checks.question: Do webhook handlers accept events without validating signature, timestamp, and source (webhook signature not verified)? (API-017)

onYes.title: Fix unverified webhooks (API-017): verify signature, timestamp, and source
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Unverified webhooks let anyone forge events, triggering unauthorized actions.

Find all instances: Search webhook handlers for signature verification, timestamp freshness, source validation, and body-integrity checks.

Fix correctly: Verify the signature over the raw body using a constant-time comparison, check timestamp freshness, validate the event source, and reject otherwise.

Constraints: Never hand-roll crypto; use the provider's vetted verification. Combine with replay protection (IAM-019).

Acceptance: Unsigned/forged webhooks are rejected. Add a test with an invalid signature proving rejection and a valid one accepted.

checks.question: Do webhook handlers assume one delivery, ordered delivery, or no retries (webhook retry/order/dedup missing)? (API-018)

onYes.title: Fix webhook delivery assumptions (API-018): idempotent, dedup, reorder-safe
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Webhooks are typically at-least-once and unordered; assuming otherwise causes duplicates/corruption.

Find all instances: Search webhook handlers for dedup, idempotency, and ordering handling.

Fix correctly: Make handlers idempotent, deduplicate by event ID, and tolerate reordering (sequence/version checks).

Constraints: Combine with CON-016/CON-017/CON-018.

Acceptance: Duplicate/out-of-order webhooks are safe. Add a test delivering duplicate and out-of-order events asserting correct final state.

checks.question: Do integrations collapse all third-party failures into generic errors without preserving actionable category/code/retryability (third-party error detail discarded)? (API-019)

onYes.title: Fix discarded third-party error detail (API-019): preserve safe cause/category
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Collapsing third-party errors loses information needed to retry correctly and debug.

Find all instances: Search integration error handling that maps all failures to one generic error.

Fix correctly: Preserve a safe, machine-readable cause/category and retryability from the third party; map to your error model accordingly.

Constraints: Don't leak sensitive third-party details to end users (ERR-014). Use the info to drive retry decisions (ERR-005).

Acceptance: Third-party error category/retryability is preserved. Add a test asserting distinct upstream failures map to distinct, actionable categories.

checks.question: Does code assume optional third-party features, versions, limits, regions, or permissions exist without feature-detection or capability negotiation (unsupported dependency capability assumed)? (API-020)

onYes.title: Fix assumed dependency capability (API-020): feature-detect or fail clearly
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Assuming a dependency capability that may be absent causes runtime failures in some environments.

Find all instances: Search for use of optional third-party features/versions/limits/regions/permissions without checking availability.

Fix correctly: Feature-detect or negotiate capability, or fail fast with a clear configuration error when unavailable.

Constraints: Config over hardcoding for capability assumptions. Fail closed where security-relevant.

Acceptance: Missing capabilities are detected or clearly reported. Add a test simulating an unsupported capability asserting graceful detection/error.
